ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: In Chhattisgarh, against a projected demand of five lakh urban dwelling units under PMAY-Urban, only 2.07 lakh units had been completed as of April 2025; audit also noted delayed planning and substantial curtailment of sanctioned projects.
parameter: Completion of dwelling units against projected demand
claimed: Demand for five lakh dwelling units was projected in the approved Housing for All Plans of Action
actual: 2.07 lakh dwelling units completed as of April 2025

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
finding: The audit found non-coverage of a considerable percentage of targeted beneficiaries under POSHAN Abhiyaan in Odisha.
parameter: Non-coverage of beneficiaries
actual: 73 to 94 percent coverage

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
finding: A short delivery of wheat to Anganwadi Centres by the appointed Transport Agent was observed during the audit.
parameter: Short delivery of wheat by Transport Agent

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
finding: Audit detected diversion of Take Home Ration (THR) funds for unrelated expenditure.
parameter: Diversion of THR cost towards other expenditure
claimed: THR funds to be used only for THR supply
actual: THR cost diverted to excess payment for SHG charges

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
finding: Bank account details on the Skill India Portal were missing, blank, null, or invalid for 90.66 lakh out of 95.90 lakh certified beneficiaries under PMKVY 2.0 and 3.0 — 94.53% of all records. Invalid entries included placeholder values such as '11111111111', '123456', single-digit numbers, and text/names/special characters. 12,122 account numbers were reused across 52,381 different candidates; one account number was shared by 2,106 individuals.
parameter: Beneficiary data integrity — bank account records on Skill India Portal
actual: 90.66 lakh (94.53%) had missing or invalid bank data

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: The Uttar Pradesh audit found delayed and inadequate release and utilisation of SBM(U) funds, weak planning and capacity building, and poor performance in segregation, processing and scientific disposal.
parameter: Release and utilisation of SBM(U) funds and achievement of urban solid-waste-management outcomes
claimed: Funds were to be released to ULBs under the SWM, capacity-building and IEC components in accordance with SBM(U) plans.
actual: During 2016-22, the share of available SWM funds released to ULBs ranged from 0 to 63 percent; release under capacity building and administrative expenses ranged from 0 to 20 percent, while IEC and public-awareness releases ranged from 3 to 62 percent. Test-checked ULBs also had substantial unutilised balances and delays in State-level fund release.

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
finding: Certified training was claimed by multiple defunct companies on the Skill India Portal. Radiate Designs (struck off by Registrar of Companies in 2015) certified 15,218 people. Neelima Moving Pictures (shut for 5–6 years) claimed to have trained 33,000 people. Present Media Private Limited certified 19,561 candidates as dancers, hairdressers, and makeup artists across nine states. At least one training partner (Jaipur Cultural Society) claimed to have conducted training on 31st February — a date that does not exist. Identical photographs were submitted as training evidence in multiple states simultaneously (Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan).
parameter: Ghost training centres and fraudulent certification

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
finding: Thousands of underage candidates were enrolled and certified in violation of PMKVY eligibility criteria. Over 52,000 candidates were certified as Group Farming Practitioners without meeting the minimum age requirement. Over 40,000 underage candidates were certified as Self-Employed Tailors. Similar violations were found across multiple other job roles. DBT incentive payments of ₹500 had not been received by 34 lakh certified candidates as of October 2024, despite the relevant phases having formally concluded. DBT was successful for only 18.44% of certified candidates as of 2023.
parameter: Underage enrolments and DBT payment failures
claimed: 95.90 lakh certified candidates to receive ₹500 DBT incentive
actual: Only 18.44% received DBT in 2023; 34 lakh unpaid as of Oct 2024

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
finding: Out of 56 lakh candidates certified under the Short-Term Training and Special Projects components of PMKVY, only 23 lakh candidates were placed, representing 41 per cent placement.
parameter: Placement of candidates certified under PMKVY
actual: 23 lakh placed candidates

schemeName: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
finding: CAG found government's claim of electrifying all 18,452 villages used a definition requiring only 10% of households to have power. Actual household electrification was 77% at the time of the ODF declaration. 3.3 crore households in "electrified" villages had no connection.
parameter: Village electrification vs household access
actual: Only 10% households needed for "electrified" status

schemeName: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
finding: CAG survey in 21 states found rural households received average of 12.5 hours electricity per day despite target of 24 hours. In UP, Bihar and Jharkhand, average supply was 6-8 hours. Rs 2,300 crore of infrastructure was stranded due to state DISCOM non-payment.
parameter: Supply quality and hours in rural areas
actual: 12.5 hours average supply

schemeName: Ayushman Bharat – PM Jan Arogya Yojana
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
finding: The audit found substantial shortfalls in beneficiary verification and coverage under AB-PMJAY in Bihar. Against the revised target of 61.8 million beneficiaries, only 25.6 million had been verified by 31 March 2024. In addition, 595 villages with eligible beneficiaries had no Ayushman Cards issued.
parameter: AB-PMJAY beneficiary verification and coverage
claimed: Coverage target of 12.1 million beneficiary families, representing approximately 61.8 million beneficiaries
actual: Only 25.6 million beneficiaries verified by 31 March 2024; 595 eligible villages had no Ayushman Card holders

finding: Punjab reported achieving functional tap connections for 100 per cent of rural households, but CAG found inaccurate and unstructured Annual Action Plans, unrealistic targets, underutilisation of funds, inadequate sustainability measures, weak operation and maintenance arrangements, and insufficient water-quality monitoring.
parameter: Functional Household Tap Connection coverage and scheme implementation
claimed: 100 per cent rural household coverage by 5 April 2023
actual: The reported achievement could not be reliably supported because planning data were inaccurate and key implementation and monitoring deficiencies persisted

finding: In Chhattisgarh, deficiencies in planning, fund management, scheme execution and water-quality monitoring resulted in non-achievement of the Jal Jeevan Mission's primary output and intended outcomes.
parameter: Achievement of programme output and outcome
actual: The primary output and outcome targets were not achieved; CAG also found mismatched data, delayed or short fund transfers, excess payments and shortfalls in water-quality testing

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: An SBM (Urban) solid waste management project of Lumding Municipal Board remained unfruitful despite fund availability; inadequate follow-up and payment of an unsecured advance led to unfruitful expenditure of ₹30.51 lakh.
parameter: Completion and productive utilisation of the solid waste management project
actual: ₹30.51 lakh incurred as unfruitful expenditure

schemeName: Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana)
finding: The Union-level performance audit found systemic deficiencies in DDUGJY and Saubhagya implementation, including incomplete electrification, weak planning and monitoring, financial irregularities, inadequate quality assurance and failure to fully achieve scheme objectives.
parameter: Achievement of rural infrastructure, household electrification, financial management and quality-assurance objectives
actual: CAG identified deficiencies across implementation, financial management, quality assurance and monitoring of Saubhagya projects in test-checked States and Union Territories.

schemeName: Saubhagya (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana)
finding: Uttar Pradesh issued an indent for electrification of 1.70 crore un-electrified households, but REC approved only 1.22 crore connections; the audit also found that off-grid connections were omitted from DPRs and identified irregularities in execution and beneficiary selection.
parameter: Households proposed for electrification versus connections approved under Saubhagya

finding: In Maharashtra, tap connections from private or own sources were included in Jal Jeevan Mission coverage even though their functionality was not established. In six test-checked districts, 9.64 lakh such connections were included in the dashboard total.
parameter: Reported tap-connection coverage under JJM
claimed: 37.89 lakh tap connections shown on the JJM dashboard in six selected districts
actual: 9.64 lakh connections were from private or own sources and could not be counted as verified JJM Functional Household Tap Connections

finding: In Madhya Pradesh, CAG found systemic planning and implementation weaknesses, including absence of baseline surveys in all test-checked districts, deficient action plans, non-prioritisation of villages, irregular expenditure, excess payments, delays, inadequate water-quality testing and failure to achieve programme outputs and outcomes.
parameter: Planning, implementation and achievement of JJM outputs and outcomes
actual: Baseline surveys were not conducted in any test-checked district and significant deficiencies affected planning, fund management, construction, monitoring and water-quality assurance

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: Out of 18 test-checked ULBs, Detailed Project Reports were prepared by only six ULBs under ISWM/SBM 1.0 and 11 ULBs under SBM 2.0. In three test-checked ULBs where DPRs were prepared, the prescribed waste-generation assessment method was not followed.
parameter: Detailed Project Reports and waste-generation assessment under SBM
actual: DPRs prepared by 6 ULBs under ISWM/SBM 1.0 and 11 ULBs under SBM 2.0

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: Fourteen test-checked Urban Local Bodies in Telangana failed to fully utilise funds provided under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban, leaving 37 per cent of the allocated funds unspent as of March 2022.
parameter: SBM-Urban fund utilisation
actual: 37 per cent of allocated SBM-Urban funds remained unspent.

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: In Punjab during 2021-22, approximately 4,222 metric tonnes of solid waste was generated per day and 4,207 metric tonnes per day was collected, but only 1,471 metric tonnes per day was treated, leaving nearly two-thirds of collected waste untreated.
parameter: Solid waste collection and treatment
actual: Only 1,471 TPD of 4,207 TPD collected waste was treated.

finding: Of the total 4,04,404 Functional Household Tap Connections disconnected during the audit period, 2,13,991 were disconnected within one month of being provided, indicating disinterest of beneficiaries in the scheme.
parameter: Sustainability and continuity of Functional Household Tap Connections
actual: 2,13,991 of 4,04,404 disconnected connections were disconnected within one month

finding: The State Ganga Committee and State Mission for Clean Ganga did not plan and implement sewage treatment infrastructure in collaboration with local communities. Many Sewage Treatment Plants remained unconnected or only partially connected to household sewer networks, existing treatment capacity was insufficient, and significant quantities of untreated sewage were discharged into the Ganga. Eighteen STPs were not taken over by the maintenance agency because of operational and safety-related deficiencies.
parameter: Sewage treatment infrastructure and operation of Sewage Treatment Plants

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
finding: The audit found that adherence to PMKVY guidelines relating to biometric attendance, insurance of candidates, organising Kaushal Melas, and training linked to captive placements was not maintained or complied with; monitoring, inspection and internal control mechanisms were also ineffective.
parameter: PMKVY guideline compliance, monitoring and internal controls

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
finding: The report included a Subject Specific Compliance Audit on Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 2.0 under the Skill Development and Employment Department, Government of Uttarakhand.
parameter: PMKVY 2.0 compliance

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: Against 135 goals specified in the Smart City Proposals of Karnataka's smart cities, achievement was 68 goals; other projects were still in progress. Smart cities also dropped 161 of 544 originally planned projects, equivalent to 30 per cent, contrary to Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs instructions.
parameter: Achievement of Smart Cities Mission goals and project retention
claimed: 135 goals specified in the Smart City Proposals
actual: 68 goals achieved

ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: Dehradun Smart City Limited identified 33 projects valued at ₹1,359.80 crore under the revised Smart City Proposal, but only 22 projects valued at ₹1,021.54 crore were implemented under the Smart Cities Mission by March 2023. The audit further found that numerous smart solutions were dropped or remained non-functional and observed wasteful expenditure of ₹6.17 crore.
parameter: Project implementation under Dehradun Smart Cities Mission
actual: 22 projects implemented

schemeName: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)
ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: The State Urban Development Agency reported that Mission cities had achieved 36-37 reform milestones, whereas Audit found that only 15-16 milestones had actually been achieved.
parameter: AMRUT reform milestones achieved
actual: 15-16 milestones

schemeName: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)
ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
finding: Although the primary objective of AMRUT was universal coverage in water supply, none of the nine mission cities achieved this objective as of October 2024. Household water-supply coverage ranged from 9.39 per cent to 89.16 per cent.
parameter: Household water-supply coverage
actual: 9.39% to 89.16% across the nine mission cities; none achieved universal coverage

ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
finding: The audit reviewed implementation of the Common Service Centres 2.0 Project under the Digital India Programme and reported shortcomings in the delivery of the project’s intended last-mile digital services.
parameter: Implementation of Common Service Centres 2.0 Project
claimed: Establishment of 2.5 lakh Common Service Centres at Gram Panchayat level

ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
finding: The audit examined the National Knowledge Network Project, a MeitY project associated with the Digital India ecosystem. The project had been approved with an outlay of ₹5,990 crore to connect 1,500 institutions.
parameter: National Knowledge Network connectivity

finding: The utilisation of funds ranged between 44 and 50 per cent under the Samagra Shiksha Scheme.
parameter: Samagra Shiksha fund utilisation
actual: Fund utilisation ranged between 44 and 50 per cent

finding: Savings of ₹1,300 crore, representing 84.20 per cent of the net grant, occurred under the scheme Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (Elementary Education) (Central Share).
parameter: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan central-share expenditure
actual: ₹1,300 crore remained unspent, equal to 84.20 per cent of the net grant

finding: Major components of Samagra Shiksha were not implemented in the test-checked districts for want of funds. Strengthening of existing schools was not undertaken in Bankura during 2019-20 to 2023-24, in Uttar Dinajpur during 2020-21 to 2023-24, in Murshidabad during 2020-21 and 2023-24, and in Dakshin Dinajpur during 2019-20 to 2021-22.
parameter: Implementation of Samagra Shiksha components
actual: Strengthening of existing schools was not implemented during the stated periods in four test-checked districts for want of funds

schemeName: PM Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM KUSUM)
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
finding: As of 31 March 2023, only 98.78 MW of solar power Power Purchase Agreements had been signed under Component A of PM-KUSUM against the State target of 500 MW, and only 3 MW had been commissioned, representing less than one per cent of the target achievement.
parameter: PM-KUSUM Component A solar power capacity implementation
actual: 3 MW commissioned

finding: The State completed construction of 34.18 lakh PMAY-G houses by March 2024 out of 34.71 lakh houses sanctioned during 2016-17 to 2022-23; deficiencies were observed in implementation of the scheme.
parameter: Construction completion of sanctioned PMAY-G houses
actual: 34.18 lakh houses completed by March 2024

finding: The Cluster Facilitation Project, aimed at improving performance in aspirational districts, remained largely ineffective due to delays in operationalisation, under-deployment of Thematic Experts, and poor achievement of performance deliverables despite payment of ₹6.56 crore. Only 11 per cent of the Thematic Experts were appointed.
parameter: Cluster Facilitation Project implementation and deployment of Thematic Experts
actual: Only 11 per cent of Thematic Experts were appointed; the project remained largely ineffective despite payment of ₹6.56 crore.

finding: The Market Board received ₹138.94 crore from the Government of India during 2017-18 to 2021-22 for implementation of three centrally sponsored schemes, including Electronic National Agriculture Market (e-NAM).
parameter: e-NAM funding received
actual: ₹138.94 crore received for implementation of e-NAM, RKVY and Bundelkhand Package

schemeName: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)
finding: The objective of separating agriculture and non-agriculture feeders under DDUGJY was not achieved. The audit also reported avoidable expenditure due to execution of unnecessary items and double payment for installation of meters at consumers' premises.
parameter: Feeder separation and project expenditure
actual: Feeder-separation objective not achieved; unnecessary works and double meter payments identified

finding: Non-identification of beneficiaries by Gram Panchayats led to non-implementation of 88.73 per cent of individual projects included in the Annual Plan.
parameter: Implementation of individual beneficiary projects

finding: Demand for employment from registered households did not exceed 48 per cent of the issued job cards during the audit period.
parameter: Household demand for MGNREGS employment

finding: Although the scheme provides for 100 days of guaranteed employment, households provided employment received an average of 21 days per household per year during 2019-24.
parameter: Employment days provided per household

finding: Pending liabilities of wages and material amounted to ₹1,217.05 crore.
parameter: Pending wage and material liabilities

ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
finding: Under the Sagarmala Programme, Andhra Pradesh proposed nine jetty projects and committed to bear 50 per cent of the project cost. Only one project, the Bhavani Island jetty, was approved; work was halted after execution of works worth ₹4.79 crore because the State did not release its ₹5 crore share. Of the remaining eight projects, revised DPRs were submitted for only three, while no decision was taken on the other five proposals.
parameter: Sagarmala jetty project implementation
actual: 1 project approved; work halted after ₹4.79 crore of works, with 8 remaining proposals not completed

finding: During the beneficiary survey, 44.01 per cent of beneficiaries were not enrolled in any of the insurance schemes, including PM Suraksha Bima Yojana, indicating that the State had not fulfilled its responsibility to sensitise and enrol job-card holders.
parameter: Insurance coverage of MGNREGS workers
actual: 44.01 per cent of surveyed beneficiaries were not enrolled in any insurance scheme.

finding: For Pradhanmantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, ₹148.00 crore was allotted during 2017-22, but only ₹8.77 crore was expended, covering 204,843 beneficiaries.
parameter: BOCW fund allotment and expenditure under PMJJBY

finding: The number of transactions peaked in 2021-22 primarily because of 16.57 crore e-Shram registrations for the informal workforce; however, the effectiveness of the Common Service Centres 2.0 platform was constrained by incomplete integration of State e-services.
parameter: e-SHRAM registrations and integration of State e-services
actual: Incomplete integration of State e-services constrained effectiveness

finding: The Board had data for only 2,51,385 workers, whereas cross-verification with the e-Shram portal showed 20,97,593 unorganised workers across 29 categories, other than agriculture and construction workers, registered in Karnataka.
parameter: Coverage and completeness of the unorganised-worker database
actual: 20,97,593 workers registered on the e-Shram portal

finding: The Government stated that 85.81 lakh workers were registered under the e-Shram portal, while registration of the remaining 59.19 lakh workers with the State welfare mechanism was still pending.
parameter: Registration of unorganised workers and convergence with State welfare schemes
claimed: 85.81 lakh workers registered under the e-Shram portal
actual: 59.19 lakh workers remained to be registered with the State welfare mechanism
